GM from the mass 0.0145 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. sources.period: Howard et al. 2025 (2025ApJS..278...52H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HOWARD_ET_AL__2025): P 16.19697 d
sources.shape: Howard et al. 2025 (2025ApJS..278...52H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HOWARD_ET_AL__2025): a/R* derived by Kepler's third law from its period 16.19697 d, stellar mass 0.67 and radius 0.696 solar units; Mayo et al. 2018 (2018AJ....155..136M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MAYO_ET_AL__2018): inclination 89.60532 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Howard et al. 2025 (2025ApJS..278...52H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HOWARD_ET_AL__2025): transit mid-time 2456991.5453 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 234 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
